# SQLx PostgreSQL source patch

This package contains the published `sqlx-postgres` 0.8.6 source from SQLx commit `bab1b022bd56a64f9a08b46b36b97c5cff19d77e`. The crates.io archive SHA-256 is `db58fcd5a53cf07c184b154801ff91347e4c30d17a3562a635ff028ad5deda46`. The original MIT and Apache licenses are included.

`PgDatabaseError::field` exposes original ErrorResponse fields. `response_length` exposes the original protocol length, including unknown fields. Both methods reuse the retained response body and preserve the driver error source. The metadata changes are in `src/error.rs` and `src/message/response.rs`. Packaging removes trailing whitespace from ordinary documentation. The JSON fixture in `src/connection/describe.rs` and SQL in `src/testing/mod.rs` use escaped literals that preserve every original input byte. A decoder regression covers localized severity, independent positions, original line text, and unknown fields.

`PgArguments::add_text` encodes PostgreSQL text-format parameters with unspecified type OID 0. Typed and text arguments share the existing rollback-capable encoder. `src/arguments.rs` retains each parameter format; `src/message/bind.rs` writes independent parameter/result format counts and correct size hints. `src/statement.rs` retains the requested parameter signature separately from server-inferred types. `src/connection/executor.rs` checks that signature before reusing cached statements or explicit metadata. Existing connection ownership, transactions, statement Close, and cache eviction remain. `src/type_info.rs` fixes strict identifier termination so `int` and `int8` do not compare equal.

Driver unit and live tests cover raw response metadata, mixed typed/text/null parameters, original encoding errors and rollback, Bind framing, cache replacement, nonpersistent queries, explicit statements, and full-width integer results. The independent protocol CI script uses one patched package identity and the same dependency family as the application.

All application dependency roots must use the coordinated SQLx PostgreSQL, SeaQuery, SeaQuery SQLx, and SeaORM patches. Cargo patches do not propagate to downstream workspace roots. The dependency preparation workflow verifies package versions, sources, and workspace exclusion. Remove the coordinated patches when upstream releases provide these capabilities and the strict PostgreSQL contracts pass against those releases.
